evidence.title: The Machines that Make the Machines
evidence.excerpt: Robotics English 한국어 中文 The Machines that Make the Machines Oct 07, 2026 By Iretiayo Akinola , Alperen Degirmenci , Yijie Guo , Hugo Hadfield , Lars Johannsmeier , Alexander Lefort , Yashraj Narang , Yichao Pan and Yixuan Wang Discuss (0) L T F R E AI-Generated Summary The NVIDIA Seattle Robotics Lab and the NVIDIA Isaac engineering team developed robotic systems to assemble GB300 tester trays, targeting busbar assembly and multi-connector insertion tasks. A classical modular pipeline using FoundationPose for perception, waypoint planning with Lissajous-curve manipulation primitives, and a high-performance impedance controller achieved over 95% success on busbar assembly with a 160-second cycle time. For multi-connector insertion, cable grasping succeeded with SAM3 segmentation, while connector grasping required a new specialist pose-estimation framework called Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited (DOPER) trained on synthetic and real-world data. Custom 3D-printed multi-purpose gripper fingers mechanically constrained part motion during contact, making grasp poses far more repeatable without tactile sensors or in-hand manipulation.
